extracted.intended_audience: Owners/operators of bulk gasoline terminals, pipeline stations, gasoline distribution facilities; environmental compliance staff; industry stakeholders and consultants; state/federal regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and implementing final NSPS and NESHAP requirements for bulk gasoline terminals, pipeline stations, and gasoline distribution facilities, including monitoring, control, definitions, recordkeeping, and electronic reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal floating roof vapor concentration limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Storage vessels with internal floating roofs must maintain the concentrations of vapors inside a storage vessel above the floating roof to less than 25 percent of the LEL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule cross-references LEL testing requirements in NESHAP subpart R. EPA is making minor revisions to the proposed test method procedures to clarify and add flexibility in response to comments, and is adding and revising corresponding recordkeeping and reporting requirements. Rationale: LEL monitoring is a development in practices that helps ensure the internal floating roof is operating effectively to reduce emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed-roof pressure relief device opening pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed roof storage vessels must have pressure relief valves with opening pressures set no less than 18 inches of water column (0.65 psig).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This revises the previously proposed 2.5 psig minimum to 18 inches of water column based on comments and rationale discussed in the preamble (section III.A.1.c.iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Major source equipment-leak monitoring frequency (NESHAP Subpart R)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require semiannual instrument monitoring of all equipment in gasoline service using either OGI according to proposed appendix K or EPA Method 21.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also require repair of any leaks identified from a monitoring event or any leaks identified by AVO methods during normal duties. Facilities will have 3 years from promulgation to comply with the semi-annual instrument monitoring requirement. EPA concluded semiannual instrument monitoring is cost-effective for major source gasoline distribution facilities (incremental cost compared to annual instrument monitoring considered reasonable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Area source equipment-leak monitoring frequency (NESHAP Subpart BBBBBB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require annual instrument monitoring of all equipment in gasoline service using either OGI according to proposed appendix K or EPA Method 21.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also require repair of any leaks identified from a monitoring event or any leaks identified by AVO methods during normal duties. EPA determined annual monitoring is cost-effective for area sources and will provide 3 years for compliance. EPA considered higher per-component costs for small/remote facilities and accounted for fixed and variable cost elements in its analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSPS Subpart XXa equipment-leak monitoring frequency (new/modified/reconstructed bulk gasoline terminals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quarterly instrument monitoring of all equipment in gasoline service using OGI according to proposed appendix K OR quarterly instrument monitoring of pumps, valves, and pressure relief devices and annual monitoring of connectors using EPA Method 21.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require repair of any leaks identified from a monitoring event or any leaks identified by AVO methods during normal duties. Agency finalized quarterly monitoring because it found the frequency cost-effective for VOC emission reductions at affected facilities. The affected facility definition was revised (see affected-facility split into 'gasoline loading rack affected facility' and 'collection of equipment at a bulk gasoline terminal affected facility').

rubrics_metrics.name: Repair requirement for identified leaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Repair of any leaks identified from an instrument monitoring event or any leaks identified by AVO methods during normal duties is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This repair obligation is specified across NESHAP Subparts R/BBBBBB and NSPS Subpart XXa in conjunction with the monitoring requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: OGI monitoring procedures and appendix K viewing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: OGI monitoring according to proposed appendix K requires viewing each component from 2 angles for 2 seconds per angle (4 seconds per component) and includes technician break requirements (a 5-minute break after 30 minutes of viewing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA used these appendix K assumptions to set an OGI monitoring rate (kept at 750 components/hour in the equipment leaks model, accounting for the viewing time and breaks). Appendix K was available for public comment and EPA finalized use of appendix K as proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance timelines for instrument monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities subject to the new instrument monitoring requirements will have up to 3 years from promulgation to comply with the instrument monitoring requirements (semiannual for major sources; annual for area sources; timelines noted for NSPS affected facilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA indicated facilities may begin instrument monitoring prior to the end of the 3-year period to avoid contractor supply issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of SSM exemption / continuous standards requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove SSM (startup, shutdown, malfunction) exemptions so that standards apply at all times; EPA is finalizing removal of SSM provisions in affected NESHAP and NSPS subparts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court precedent (Sierra Club v. EPA) requires emissions standards to be continuous in nature. The EPA interprets CAA sections 111 and 112 as not requiring emissions during malfunctions to be factored into standard development, but SSM exemptions previously present are being removed. The agency accommodated predictable startup and shutdown periods in final standards rather than having SSM exemptions; malfunctions remain distinct (sudden, infrequent, not reasonably preventable) and are not factored into developing the standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic reporting requirements (CDX/CEDRI/ERT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners and operators of bulk gasoline terminals subject to NSPS subpart XXa and gasoline distribution facilities subject to NESHAP subparts R and BBBBBB must submit electronic copies of required performance test reports, performance evaluation reports, semiannual reports, and Notification of Compliance Status reports through EPA's CDX using CEDRI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance test results supported by the EPA's Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT) at the time of the test must be submitted in the ERT-generated format or an electronic file consistent with the ERT xml schema; other performance test results must be submitted in PDF using the ERT attachment module. Performance evaluation results of CEMS measuring RATA pollutants supported by the ERT must be submitted similarly. Semiannual reports require use of the appropriate spreadsheet template hosted on CEDRI. Notification of Compliance Status reports must be submitted as a PDF upload. NSPS Subpart XXa includes provisions allowing owners/operators to seek extensions for submitting electronic reports for circumstances beyond control (CDX/CEDRI outage, force majeure), with a process to assert such claims; similar extensions are codified in 40 CFR part 63, subpart A for NESHAPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability determination transition and retention of certain definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition away from applicability equations in 40 CFR 63.420 to applicability determined solely based on major source determination over a 3-year period; proposed deletions of 'controlled loading rack' and 'uncontrolled loading rack' definitions are not being finalized until applicability equations are no longer available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA retained the 'controlled/uncontrolled loading rack' definitions to define terms while applicability equations remain available and is otherwise finalizing the transition away from the equations as proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of bulk gasoline terminal (facility-level throughput)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final definition of 'bulk gasoline terminal' in NESHAP subpart BBBBBB: any gasoline facility with gasoline throughput of 20,000 gallons per day (75,700 liters per day) or greater (facility-level throughput).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA clarified that the 20,000 gpd threshold is evaluated based on total facility gasoline throughput (including pipeline throughput) so co-located operations are appropriately classified for applicable requirements. For major sources, meeting threshold may trigger loading operations to meet 10 mg/L TOC limit in NESHAP subpart R; area sources have separate throughput-based requirements in BBBBBB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of pipeline breakout station and loading-rack clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: Pipeline breakout stations do not have loading racks where gasoline is loaded into cargo tanks. If only diesel loading occurs, the facility is considered a pipeline station; loading racks used to load gasoline into cargo tanks make the facility a bulk gasoline terminal for the subpart if facility-wide gasoline throughput exceeds thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA added the clarifying phrase 'where gasoline is loaded into cargo tanks' to avoid classifying facilities with non-gasoline loading racks as bulk gasoline terminals. The parenthetical '(including pipeline throughput)' intentionally requires facility-level evaluation of gasoline throughput.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of gasoline (include RVP in psi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise definition of 'gasoline' in NESHAP subpart BBBBBB to include Reid vapor pressure in units of pounds per square inch (psi) as well as kilopascals; add same definition directly in NESHAP subpart R rather than relying on NSPS subpart XX/XXa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change is minor and aligns the rule with units commonly used in the U.S. gasoline distribution industry; EPA received no comments and is finalizing as proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of submerged filling
rubrics_metrics.description: Add definition of 'submerged filling' to NESHAP subpart R similar to the definition in NESHAP subpart BBBBBB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalizing the added definition as proposed, with the exception of removing the phrase 'for the purposes of this subpart' from NSPS subpart XXa and NESHAP subpart R. Submerged fill requirements were proposed to be added in NESHAP subpart R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of flare vs. thermal oxidation system and performance testing applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise definitions of 'flare' and 'thermal oxidation system' to clarify that thermal oxidation systems 'emit pollutants through a conveyance suitable to conduct a performance test' while flares are exempt from performance testing because they do not emit through such a conveyance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA decided not to change the historic term 'thermal oxidation system' to 'vapor combustion unit' to avoid inconsistencies with permits and prior rules. EPA is also revising instances where the phrase 'thermal oxidation system other than a flare' was used to simply say 'thermal oxidation system' because flares are not a subset of thermal oxidation systems under the final definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 63 general provisions and table entry revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise multiple entries in Table 1 to Subpart R and Table 4 to Subpart BBBBBB to correct paragraph references, typographical errors, and update applicability (e.g., revise entry for 40 CFR 63.9(f) to 'no'; revise entry for 40 CFR 63.7(e)(3) to include an exception for 40 CFR 63.11092(e); correct cross-reference for 40 CFR 63.10(b)(2)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA reviewed alternative work practice equipment leak provisions (40 CFR 63.11(c)-(e)) and concluded these provisions would not apply after full implementation of OGI monitoring under appendix K in many cases, but acknowledged discrepancies between table entries and adjusted accordingly. EPA noted Method 21 is primarily limited to vapor collection system monitoring prior to a performance test and OGI is not approved as an alternative for 'no detectable emissions' monitoring events.
